schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control

1.method: ciphers/hellen-frederick-1752/pool_stats.py on the 8 Bourdeau-audit ciphertext files: per-record segment/numeric/distinct/range/digit-width stats; cross-family Jaccard of numeric type-sets (1752 vs 1756 vs 1763-pooled); a one-key pool test on the six 1763 despatches (real pairwise Jaccard of numeric type-sets between the 6 records vs a control of 200 random re-splits of the same pooled 1234-token stream into groups of the same 6 sizes, seed 20260925).

result.interpretation_cross_family: low overlap (0.08-0.13) across the three date groups, consistent with Bourdeau's own repeated-bigram finding of three separate codes (1752, 1756, 1763) -- independently reproduced here from the audit files with a different statistic (type-set Jaccard, not bigram overlap)
result.interpretation_cluster_1763: the real six-record cross-record Jaccard (0.1456) sits at the 92nd percentile of the random-split control (only 8% of 200 chance re-splits of the same pool score higher) -- indistinguishable from what a random partition of one shared vocabulary would produce. This does NOT prove one key (a random split is not a strong discriminator on its own, and the test cannot rule out two similar but distinct codebooks with heavy overlap), but it is consistent with the pools-first hypothesis and finds no evidence against it.
